newsitem.title: USA: Voters give odds to lottery over budget balance.
newsitem.headline: Voters give odds to lottery over budget balance.

text.p: Americans believe they are more likely to buy a winning lottery ticket than Washington is to balance the federal budget, a poll released Wednesday said.

The polling company (cq lower case), a private firm which has conducted voter polls for Republican politican candidates, found 61 percent of registered voters thought they had a better chance of winning the lottery than the government did of ending nearly three decades of deficit spending.
The odds of winning the national Powerball lottery are 55 million to one.

Only 26 percent of those polled would place their bets on the government balancing the budget in the near future and 11 percent said neither event would occur, according to the telephone survey of 1,000 registered voters conducted March 17-24. The margin of error is 3.1 percent, plus or minus.
